topic: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks (2017-2024)

papers.title: Attention Is All You Need
papers.abstract: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder. The best performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train.

papers.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
papers.abstract: We introduce a new language representation model called BERT, which stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers. Unlike recent language representation models, BERT is designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers. As a result, the pre-trained BERT model can be fine-tuned with just one additional output layer to create state-of-the-art models for a wide range of tasks, such as question answering and language inference.

papers.title: FEVER: a Large-scale Dataset for Fact Extraction and VERification
papers.abstract: In this paper we introduce a new publicly available dataset for fact extraction and verification (FEVER). It consists of 185,445 claims generated by altering sentences extracted from Wikipedia and subsequently verified without knowledge of the sentence they were derived from. The claims are classified as Supported, Refuted or NotEnoughInfo by annotators who extract evidence sentences from Wikipedia. For the first time, this benchmark enables evaluating retrieval-based factual verification at scale.

papers.title: BART: Denoising Sequence-to-Sequence Pre-training for Natural Language Generation, Translation, and Comprehension
papers.abstract: We present BART, a denoising autoencoder for pretraining sequence-to-sequence models. BART is trained by corrupting text with an arbitrary noising function, and learning a model to reconstruct the original text. It uses a standard Transformer-based neural machine translation architecture. BART is particularly effective when fine tuned for text generation, and serves as the primary generator backbone in standard RAG-Token and RAG-Sequence.

papers.title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
papers.abstract: Transfer learning has emerged as a powerful technique in natural language processing. In this paper, we explore the landscape of transfer learning for NLP by introducing a unified framework that converts every language problem into a text-to-text format. Our systematic study compares pre-training objectives, architectures, unlabeled datasets, transfer approaches, and other factors on dozens of language benchmarks.

papers.title: Language Models as Knowledge Bases?
papers.abstract: Recent work has shown that pre-trained language models capture a surprising amount of syntactic and semantic information. Yet, to what extent do they store relational knowledge? In this paper we introduce the LAMA benchmark to test the factual and commonsense knowledge stored in pretrained models without fine-tuning. We find that language models can retrieve knowledge without task-specific engineering, setting the stage for comparing parametric memory against external retrieval.

papers.title: Generalization through Memorization: Nearest Neighbor Language Models
papers.abstract: We introduce kNN-LM, an approach that extends a pre-trained language model by linearly interpolating its next-word distribution with a k-nearest neighbors distribution computed over a datastore of external text representations. By augmenting language models with non-parametric nearest-neighbor memory at test time without retraining, we demonstrate substantial perplexity improvements and establish the viability of memory-augmented inference.

papers.title: Learning to Retrieve Reasoning Paths over Wikipedia Graph for Multi-hop Question Answering
papers.abstract: Answering multi-hop questions requires finding multiple evidence passages and reasoning over them. We introduce a recurrent retrieval approach that learns to retrieve reasoning paths over a Wikipedia graph. By sequentially retrieving interconnected paragraphs, our model captures multi-step evidence chains and outperforms single-shot retrieval for complex QA.

papers.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
papers.abstract: Open-domain question answering relies on efficient passage retrieval to select candidate contexts. In this work, we show that retrieval can be practically implemented using dense representations alone, where embeddings are learned from a small number of questions and passages by a simple dual-encoder framework. DPR dramatically outperforms classical BM25 and serves as the retrieval component in standard RAG.

papers.title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
papers.abstract: Language model pre-training has shown to capture a surprising amount of world knowledge. However, this knowledge is stored implicitly in neural weights. We present REALM, which augments language models with a learned neural retriever that retrieves documents from a large textual corpus during masked language model pre-training. We show how to backpropagate through the marginalization over retrieved documents.

papers.title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
papers.abstract: We propose ColBERT, a novel ranking model that adapts deep language models for efficient retrieval. ColBERT introduces a late interaction architecture that independently encodes the query and the document using BERT and then employs a cheap yet powerful MaxSim interaction step. This preserves expressiveness while maintaining sub-millisecond retrieval speeds.

papers.title: Approximate Nearest Neighbor Negative Contrastive Learning for Dense Text Retrieval
papers.abstract: Dense retrieval models often struggle when trained with static BM25 or random negative examples. We propose ANCE, which updates negative samples dynamically using the retrieval model's own approximate nearest neighbor index during training. This addresses the discrepancy between training negatives and retrieval-time negatives.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
papers.abstract: Large pre-trained language models have been shown to store factual knowledge in their parameters. However, their ability to precisely access and manipulate knowledge is still limited. We explore a general-purpose fine-tuning recipe for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)—models which combine pre-trained parametric and non-parametric memory. We introduce RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token models, which retrieve dense passage representations with DPR and generate answers with BART.

papers.title: Leveraging Passage Retrieval with Generative Models for Open Domain Question Answering
papers.abstract: Generative models for open-domain question answering have proven effective, but scaling to large numbers of retrieved passages is computationally challenging. We propose Fusion-in-Decoder (FiD), which processes each retrieved passage independently in the encoder and concatenates their representations in the decoder attention layers. This enables scaling to 100 retrieved passages without exploding computational cost.

papers.title: AmbigQA: Answering Ambiguous Open-Domain Questions
papers.abstract: Most open-domain question answering datasets assume a single unambiguous answer. We introduce AmbigQA, demonstrating that over half of open-domain questions are ambiguous. Handling ambiguity requires retrieving diverse evidence and generating conditional, disambiguated answers, exposing limitations in single-shot RAG.

papers.title: How Context Affects Language Models' Factual Predictions
papers.abstract: When language models are augmented with retrieved context, how do they resolve conflicts between their parametric memory and the external text? We systematically measure the sensitivity of language models to external evidence and demonstrate that providing noisy or conflicting retrieved context often leads to model hallucinations.

papers.title: End-to-End Training of Multi-Document Reader and Retriever for Open-Domain Question Answering
papers.abstract: In standard RAG, the retriever is either frozen or trained separately from the multi-document reader. We propose EMDR2, an expectation-maximization approach that trains both the dense retriever and the Fusion-in-Decoder reader end-to-end, treating retrieved passages as latent variables and maximizing marginal answer likelihood.

papers.title: Retrieval Augmentation Reduces Hallucination in Conversation
papers.abstract: Conversational neural language models frequently generate convincing but factually incorrect statements (hallucinations). We show that conditioning generation on retrieved passages from a large corpus significantly reduces factual hallucinations, demonstrating the safety and grounding benefits of RAG in conversational settings.

papers.title: Towards Unsupervised Dense Information Retrieval with Contriever
papers.abstract: Dense retrieval models generally require large amounts of supervised question-passage pairs. We propose Contriever, a contrastive learning method for unsupervised dense information retrieval. Contriever achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot retrieval and becomes the standard general-purpose retriever for LLM RAG pipelines.

papers.title: Improving Language Models by Retrieving from Trillions of Tokens
papers.abstract: We explore retrieval augmentation at autoregressive language model scale by introducing RETRO (Retrieval-Enhanced Transformer). RETRO retrieves nearest-neighbor document chunks from a database of trillions of tokens and conditions the language model using chunked cross-attention. This enables a 7B parameter model to match the performance of a 175B model.

papers.title: Few-shot Learning with Retrieval Augmented Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models demonstrate remarkable few-shot capabilities, but their factual knowledge is limited by model size. We present Atlas, a carefully designed retrieval-augmented language model combining a dense retriever with a T5 seq2seq generator trained jointly via Attention Distillation. Atlas demonstrates superior few-shot performance on knowledge-intensive benchmarks while using significantly fewer parameters.

papers.title: When Not to Trust Language Models: Investigating Effectiveness of Parametric and Non-Parametric Memories
papers.abstract: We evaluate when language models succeed via parametric memory versus when they require external retrieval. Using PopQA, we show that large language models perform well on popular entities but fail systematically on long-tail knowledge. Retrieval augmentation disproportionately benefits long-tail queries, proving that adaptive retrieval should be query-popularity dependent.

papers.title: Measuring and Narrowing the Compositionality Gap in Language Models
papers.abstract: We investigate the ability of language models to answer compositional multi-hop questions. We introduce the Self-Ask prompting method, which decomposes a complex question into sub-questions, executes intermediate search queries, and aggregates answers sequentially. This bridges the compositionality gap and serves as a precursor to iterative retrieval-augmented reasoning.

papers.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
papers.abstract: While language models exhibit strong reasoning via Chain-of-Thought, their reasoning is disconnected from external environments. We propose ReAct, where LLMs alternate between generating reasoning traces and task-specific actions such as querying a search engine. This synergy drastically reduces hallucination and makes multi-step retrieval accessible without fine-tuning.

papers.title: On the Origin of Hallucinations in Conversational Models: Data-Traceability and Grounding
papers.abstract: We investigate why neural conversational models hallucinate unsupported facts. We demonstrate that token-level hallucination stems from weak semantic grounding and show that ungrounded models produce fabricated facts over 60% of the time. We establish fine-grained token-level attribution metrics essential for evaluating retrieval-grounded text.

papers.title: REPLUG: Retrieval-Augmented Black-Box Language Models
papers.abstract: Existing RAG methods either require training internal parameters or rely on lightweight prompts. We propose REPLUG, a framework that treats the target language model as a black box. REPLUG prepends retrieved documents in parallel, computes ensemble output distributions, and tunes the dense retriever using the black-box LM's cross-entropy loss as supervision.

papers.title: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation
papers.abstract: Standard RAG retrieves documents once at the beginning of generation. For long or complex outputs, retrieval must happen dynamically when the model is uncertain. We propose FLARE (Forward-Looking Active REtrieval), which anticipates future generation and iteratively triggers retrieval only when generated sentence tokens have low generation confidence.

papers.title: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy
papers.abstract: Retrieval and generation should inform each other iteratively. We introduce ITER-RETGEN, an iterative framework where retrieved documents assist in generating text, and the generated text in turn serves as context to retrieve more relevant documents. This synergistic cycle significantly improves performance on complex multi-hop QA.

papers.title: Interleaving Retrieval with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Knowledge-Intensive Multi-Step Questions
papers.abstract: Answering multi-step questions requires both step-by-step reasoning and precise external facts. We introduce IRCoT (Interleaving Retrieval with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning), which uses intermediate CoT sentences as retrieval queries to fetch supporting paragraphs, which in turn guide the next reasoning step.

papers.title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
papers.abstract: Despite the success of RAG, indiscriminately retrieving passages hurts performance when retrieval is unnecessary or retrieved passages are noisy. We introduce Self-RAG, a framework where a language model learns to dynamically retrieve on-demand and evaluate its own output using special reflection tokens ([Retrieve], [IsREL], [IsSUP], [IsUSE]). Self-RAG adaptively controls retrieval frequency and factual consistency.

papers.title: Generate rather than Retrieve: Large Language Models are Strong Context Generators
papers.abstract: Can language models generate their own context instead of retrieving from an external corpus? We propose GenRead, an alternative to standard RAG where an LLM first generates background documents about the query before answering. We analyze the tradeoffs between parametric generation and non-parametric retrieval.

papers.title: RECOMP: Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Compression and Selective Augmentation
papers.abstract: Retrieved documents often contain substantial irrelevant text that consumes context windows and confuses language models. We propose RECOMP, which trains compressor models to compress multiple retrieved documents into concise summaries before feeding them to the generation model.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
papers.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has rapidly evolved in the LLM era. This survey organizes the paradigm into Naive RAG, Advanced RAG, and Modular RAG, categorizing pre-retrieval, retrieval, post-retrieval, and generation stages. It defines the formal taxonomic vocabulary adopted across modern RAG literature.

papers.title: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation
papers.abstract: Standard RAG suffers when retrieval returns irrelevant or incorrect documents, leading to hallucination. We propose Corrective RAG (CRAG), which evaluates retrieved documents via a lightweight retrieval evaluator. If retrieval is confidence-poor, CRAG triggers web search or knowledge strip-filtering to correct the retrieved evidence before generation.

papers.title: Adaptive-RAG: Determining When to Retrieve for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Not all user queries require retrieval; simple queries can be answered from parametric memory, while complex queries need multi-step retrieval. We propose Adaptive-RAG, which employs a small classifier to determine query complexity dynamically, routing requests to no retrieval, single-step RAG, or iterative multi-hop RAG.

papers.title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
papers.abstract: Standard RAG excels at localized fact retrieval but fails on global questions requiring holistic corpus understanding. We introduce Graph RAG, which extracts knowledge graphs and community clusters from raw text to perform hierarchical summarization, answering global sensemaking queries across entire datasets.

papers.title: RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval
papers.abstract: Retrieval methods typically retrieve isolated low-level chunks. We propose RAPTOR, which recursively clusters and summarizes text chunks into a hierarchical tree representation. At inference time, RAPTOR retrieves across multiple abstraction levels, enabling both granular fact extraction and thematic synthesis.

papers.title: Speculative RAG: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Speculative Drafting
papers.abstract: Feeding large numbers of retrieved documents directly into heavy LLMs creates severe computational latency. Inspired by speculative decoding, we introduce Speculative RAG: a small draft model generates multiple candidate answers based on subsets of retrieved documents in parallel, which a larger verifier model selects and synthesizes.

papers.title: Making Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Robust to Irrelevant Documents
papers.abstract: Retrieval systems frequently retrieve irrelevant or distracter passages that degrade downstream generation accuracy. We develop training procedures that expose language models to hard distracters during fine-tuning, training the generator to explicitly ignore unhelpful or misleading passages.

papers.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
papers.abstract: We analyze how language models access information within long input contexts. We find that performance is highest when relevant information is at the very beginning or end of the input context, and degrades substantially when relevant context is positioned in the middle, fundamentally changing post-retrieval reranking strategies.

concepts.name: Self-Attention Mechanism
concepts.definition: Mechanism computing pairwise token interaction weights within a sequence, forming the foundation of modern Transformer language representations.

concepts.name: Cross-Attention Mechanism
concepts.definition: Attention mechanism conditioning decoder token representations directly on external or encoder sequence representations.

concepts.name: Pretrained Bidirectional Encoders
concepts.definition: Deep contextualized bidirectional language representations pretrained via masked language modeling, producing dense vector representations of arbitrary text.

concepts.name: External Knowledge Grounding
concepts.definition: Conditioning model outputs on verifiable external evidence sources rather than relying purely on internal parametric weights.

concepts.name: Sequence-to-Sequence Denoising
concepts.definition: Autoregressive generation architecture trained to reconstruct corrupted input text, ideal for synthesizing answers from multi-document contexts.

concepts.name: Parametric vs Non-Parametric Memory
concepts.definition: Dichotomy between static knowledge stored implicitly inside neural network weights versus dynamic knowledge retrieved on-demand from an external text datastore.

concepts.name: Dense Passage Retrieval
concepts.definition: Mapping queries and candidate text passages into a shared continuous vector space using dual encoders trained with contrastive loss to enable sub-linear maximum inner-product search.

concepts.name: Nearest Neighbor Language Modeling
concepts.definition: Linearly interpolating a neural generator's next-token output probability with a non-parametric nearest-neighbor distribution over offline datastore embeddings.

concepts.name: Late Interaction Token Matching
concepts.definition: Preserving all token-level representations of queries and documents to compute fine-grained MaxSim interaction after independent encoding.

concepts.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
concepts.definition: End-to-end framework combining a neural passage retriever with a sequence-to-sequence generator, conditioning output probability distributions on retrieved evidence.

concepts.name: Token-Level Document Marginalization
concepts.definition: Marginalizing the next-token probability distribution over top-k retrieved passages per generation step, allowing different passages to inform different tokens.

concepts.name: Sequence-Level Document Marginalization
concepts.definition: Conditioning entire generated output sequences on a single retrieved document, marginalizing probabilities across candidate sequences at the document level.

concepts.name: Fusion-in-Decoder Cross-Attention
concepts.definition: Encoding multiple retrieved passages independently and concatenating their representations inside the generative decoder cross-attention layers, scaling retrieval to 100+ documents.

concepts.name: Chunked Cross-Attention
concepts.definition: Retrieving nearest-neighbor text chunks per input chunk during autoregressive generation and conditioning decoder blocks at regular token intervals.

concepts.name: Retriever-Generator Attention Distillation
concepts.definition: Supervising a dense retriever using cross-attention scores computed by a frozen or jointly trained seq2seq generator, eliminating the need for gold retrieval annotations.

concepts.name: Long-Tail Knowledge Vulnerability
concepts.definition: Empirical phenomenon where parametric models succeed on head entity knowledge but suffer catastrophic accuracy drops on low-frequency tail entities without external retrieval.

concepts.name: Multi-Step Query Decomposition
concepts.definition: Decomposing complex, multi-hop user questions into sequential sub-questions that each trigger distinct intermediate retrieval steps.

concepts.name: Active and Confidence-Triggered Retrieval
concepts.definition: Dynamically initiating retrieval operations during generation based on model uncertainty or token generation confidence, rather than retrieving once upfront.

concepts.name: Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy
concepts.definition: Alternating multi-round pipeline where generated hypotheses inform downstream retrieval queries, and newly retrieved passages guide subsequent generation refinement.

concepts.name: Self-Reflective Retrieval and Critique
concepts.definition: Integrating special reflection and critique tokens ([Retrieve], [IsREL], [IsSUP], [IsUSE]) into the vocabulary to allow an LM to judge when retrieval is needed and critique evidence quality.

concepts.name: Post-Retrieval Context Compression
concepts.definition: Compressing or filtering retrieved passages into dense extractive or abstractive summaries before feeding them into generator context windows.

concepts.name: Corrective Retrieval and Verification
concepts.definition: Evaluating the confidence of retrieved documents with an external evaluator and dynamically falling back to web search or document strip-filtering when relevance is ambiguous.

concepts.name: Adaptive Complexity Query Routing
concepts.definition: Classifying incoming query complexity prior to execution to route requests between zero-retrieval, single-hop RAG, or iterative multi-hop pipelines.

concepts.name: Hierarchical Recursive Tree Retrieval
concepts.definition: Recursively clustering and summarizing text chunks into an abstraction tree, allowing queries to retrieve at either granular sentence levels or high-level thematic summaries.

concepts.name: Graph-Augmented Entity Retrieval
concepts.definition: Extracting entity-relationship graphs and community structures from text collections to synthesize answers for global, corpus-wide queries.
